key_insight: Targeted fine-tuning helped small open-source LLMs better identify biomedical semantic relationships, boosting average F1 by 34.1 percentage points.
clinical_relevance: Improved automatic ontology generation could speed up biomedical knowledge organization and support downstream research and clinical NLP workflows.
method: Benchmarked five open-source LLMs up to 9B parameters.
Compared standard prompting, Chain-of-Thought prompting, and fine-tuning.
Evaluated models on MeSH-Rel-4K, a 4K biomedical semantic-relationship dataset.
evidence_signal: The study used a 4,000-example MeSH-based dataset and reported that fine-tuning produced the largest gain in average F1-score across the evaluated models.
watch_item: Results come from a focused biomedical relationship task, so generalization to other ontology types, domains, or production settings may require further validation.
paper_title: Benchmarking Resource-Efficient LLMs for Research Topic Ontology Generation in the Biomedical Field
